Debian Audio Pipeline Audit — PipeWire Subversion of Firefox DSP (ALC269 Unlock) 2026-06-26 pipewire, alsa, cubeb, audiostream, dsp, alc269, sony-vaio, firefox, audio-pipeline, wireplumber
Complete audit of how PipeWire intercepts and degrades Firefox AudioStream DSP output on the Sony SVE14A3AJ, and the full resolution applied to unleash the ALC269 silicon. DSP work inside Firefox was correct but neutralized at the OS audio layer by forced resampling, a parasitic filter-chain daemon, and a cubeb double-hop through pipewire-pulse.
<pipeline> Firefox AudioStream.cpp (DSP) → cubeb → pipewire-pulse → PipeWire 1.4.2 → ALSA snd_hda_intel → ALC269 codec → SVE14A3AJ speakers </pipeline>
<problems> <problem id="1" name="Forced Resampling (PRIMARY OFFENDER)"> PipeWire was locked to only 48000 Hz via default.clock.allowed-rates = [48000]. Firefox DSP outputs at 44100 Hz. PipeWire force-resampled every stream, mathematically smoothing peaks and flattening custom bass boost and make-up gain from AudioPsychoacousticEnhancer. </problem> <problem id="2" name="filter-chain Ghost Process"> A second PipeWire daemon ran as filter-chain.service: /usr/bin/pipewire -c filter-chain.conf. Even with no EQ plugins, it inserted a libpipewire-module-adapter resampler node into the audio graph — an extra conversion hop degrading signal fidelity. </problem> <problem id="3" name="cubeb Double-Hop via pipewire-pulse"> mozconfig had ac_add_options --with-system-pipewire, causing cubeb to route through the PulseAudio shim (pipewire-pulse). Route: Firefox → PulseAudio layer → PipeWire → speakers. Two hops with extra normalization potential. </problem> </problems>
<hardware> <device>Sony SVE14A3AJ — Intel HDA PCH — Realtek ALC269</device> <native_rates>44100, 48000, 96000, 192000 Hz</native_rates> <native_bits>16-bit, 20-bit, 24-bit</native_bits> <pipewire_node>alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1b.0.analog-stereo</pipewire_node> <note>Hardware had ZERO limitations. PipeWire config was the entire bottleneck.</note> <verified_via>/proc/asound/card0/codec#0 and pw-dump</verified_via> </hardware>
<resolution> <fix name="PipeWire Clock Unlock"> File: ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/10-unleashed.conf Set default.clock.allowed-rates = [44100 48000 96000 192000]. PipeWire now switches master clock dynamically. Zero forced resampling for native rates. </fix> <fix name="WirePlumber Hardware Policy"> File: ~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/10-alc269.conf Matched alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1b.0.analog-stereo node explicitly. Unlocked all native rates, upgraded bit depth to S24LE (true 24-bit native), enabled api.alsa.multi-rate, disabled batch mode for better HDA timing accuracy. </fix> <fix name="filter-chain.service Killed"> Command: systemctl --user disable --now filter-chain.service Parasitic second PipeWire process permanently gone. Now 3 clean daemons only. </fix> <fix name="Resample Quality Maximized"> File: ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire-pulse.conf.d/10-unleashed.conf resample.quality = 15 — maximum quality IF resampling ever occurs. </fix> </resolution>
<audiostream_v2> <canonical>/home/gorilla/Documents/FIrefox.153.Work/GitHub_Staging/Firefox_Unleashed_Zeroa_CPU/patches/Last.tweaks/AudioStream_v2/AudioStream.cpp</canonical> <deployed>/home/gorilla/Documents/FIrefox.153.Work/patches/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp</deployed> <timestamp>2026-06-25 22:10</timestamp> <size_bytes>35737</size_bytes> <diff_status>ZERO DIFF — perfect match verified</diff_status> <v2_fixes> 1. Always-active fixed gains: mBassBoostGain=1.8f, mXLoudBoost=0.6f (dynamic linking made DSP inert) 2. Pure tanh SoftClip — fixed piecewise threshold bug that caused harmonic artifacts 3. xLOUD drive reduced from 0.9 to 0.6 (0.9 caused distortion at loud volumes) 4. UpdateGains() hardened to always-on fixed values </v2_fixes> <archive_docs>/home/gorilla/Documents/FIrefox.153.Work/GitHub_Staging/Firefox_Unleashed_Zeroa_CPU/patches/Last.tweaks/AudioStream_v2/ARCHIVE_DOCS/</archive_docs> </audiostream_v2>
<lesson> Always audit the full signal chain end-to-end. DSP work inside Firefox runs correctly but can be neutralized at the OS audio layer. Hardware capability is NOT the same as software configuration. Verify with pw-dump and /proc/asound/card0/codec#0 to see what the silicon actually supports vs what the software allows. </lesson>
[AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-02 — HISTORICAL-TRUE + 2 corrected claims] the end-to-end audit METHOD here is true and canonized 2026-08-02. Two claims were later corrected: the S24LE 'upgrade' was itself the no-sound bug (driver exposes S16/S32 only — see pipewire_s24le_format_rejection); filter-chain 'disabled' was insufficient (Debian preset resurrects it — mask required). xLOUD 0.6 was an intermediate value (current 0.4).
